To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an inwardly rectified whole cell current is activated by store depletion in oocytes expressing G(q)-coupling receptors.
a constitutively activated Ca(2+) current was observed in cells expressing G(q)-couple receptors, and that this current was induced by Ca(2+) release from the endoplasmic reticulum.
an inwardly rectified Ca(2+)-(dependent) whole cell current is activated after Gq-coupling receptor-induced Ca(2+) release from the ER, and that this current is not mediated by P2Y(2)-receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of G protein-couple receptors in Ca(2) entry in Xenopus laevis oocytes.
the regulation and functional significance of a whole cell inwardly rectifying K(+) current induced by G protein-coupling receptors.
the regulation and function of an inwardly-rectifying current in Xenopus oocyte.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this current is not a P2Y( 1)-receptor current, but rather a Ca(2+)(i)-activated whole cell current that is induced by G(q)-couple receptors.
this inwardly rectifying K(+) current is activated after Ca(2+) release from intracellular stores, which is induced by G(q)-coupling of the expressed receptors.
the inwardly rectifying currents described here are likely to represent a novel Ca(2+)(i)-dependent whole cell current, which may be important for Ca(2+) homeostasis in oocytes and other cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the G(q)-dependent inwardly rectifying currents in oocytes is a consequence of the G protein coupling and not of the receptor subtype.
this current is activated in response to G(q) protein activation and Ca(2+) release from intracellular Ca(2+) stores.
the inwardly rectifying Ca(2+)(i)-dependent whole cell current in oocytes is induced by store depletion and may play a role in Ca (2+) entry after receptor stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we discovered a new inwardly rectifying K+ current in the Xenopus oocyte.
we have discovered an inwardly rectified current that is activated by G(q)-couple receptors and Ca(2+) release from intracellular stores.
G protein-coupling to G(q) is not sufficient for receptor-independent Ca(2+)(i) entry in oocytes.
